caller_is_authorized.meaning: the caller of rebalanceFunds() is an authorized party rather than a random EOA

rebalance_callable_by_anyone.meaning: rebalanceFunds() is externally callable with no access control by any address

excess_liquidity_present.meaning: excess liquidity above the target buffer exists on-chain after a large mint

target_buffer_configured.meaning: the vault is configured to retain only an exact target buffer on-chain

fast_redemption_disabled.meaning: subsequent redemptions are forced onto the slow off-chain custodian path, disabling the fast redemption feature

assumptions: No funds are stolen; the issue is griefing / denial-of-service (as_no_funds_stolen).
The large mint and excess liquidity are a conditional scenario, not an observed on-chain event.
The 5% target buffer is an illustrative example, not a verified configuration value.
The issuer manual top-up mechanism and its timing are not specified.

unresolved.description: Report does not establish that a large mint or excess liquidity actually occurred before the call; it is a conditional scenario, so the excess-liquidity precondition is treated as a scenario qualifier rather than an observed fact.
The exact target buffer percentage (5%) is given only as an example, not a verified configuration; no numeric buffer value is bound.
The report does not identify which parties are authorized to call rebalanceFunds(); authorization is represented as a grounded Boolean rather than a concrete role or address.

limitations: Only the direct impact i_fast_redemptions_disabled is formalized; i_ux_destroyed and i_drain_when_needed are deferred to future claims.
Authorization is encoded as a Boolean because the report does not define the authorized caller set or role.
The target buffer is not bound to a numeric value; the 5% figure is illustrative only.
Code-level binding of caller_is_authorized and fast_redemption_disabled is deferred.
